children.label: Vertically Opposite Angles and Linear Pairs

tooltip_popover.title: Vertically Opposite Angles and Linear Pairs
tooltip_popover.description: Two straight lines intersect at at most one unique point, forming four angles.
tooltip_popover.example: If intersecting angle a = 35°, adjacent angle b = 180° - 35° = 145°, vertically opposite angle c = 35°, angle d = 145°.

tooltip_popover.title: Equidistant Parallelism and Orthogonality
tooltip_popover.description: Parallel lines lie in the same plane and never meet, maintaining constant perpendicular distance throughout.
tooltip_popover.example: Opposite edges of a ruler, railway tracks.

tooltip_popover.title: Paper Folding Constructions
tooltip_popover.description: Successive parallel horizontal paper folds produce parallel line creases.
tooltip_popover.example: Folding square paper in half repeatedly creates parallel grid line creases.

image_asset.title: Intersecting Lines, Parallel Lines & Crease Geometry Diagram
image_asset.description: Vertically opposite angles, linear pairs, parallel line constant distance, perpendicular lines, and crease geometry.

hotspots.title: Intersecting Lines & Angles
hotspots.popover_content: Vertically opposite angles are equal (∠a = ∠c). Linear pairs sum to 180° (∠a + ∠b = 180°).

hotspots.title: Parallel Lines (l || m)
hotspots.popover_content: Coplanar lines that never meet. Maintain constant perpendicular distance throughout.

hotspots.title: Perpendicular Lines (l ⊥ m)
hotspots.popover_content: Lines that intersect at right angles (90°), forming 4 orthogonal quadrants.

hotspots.title: Paper Folding Creases
hotspots.popover_content: Successive horizontal folds yield parallel line creases; orthogonal fold creates perpendicular crease.
